3. The case of the prosecution can be summarized as under:
3.1. The original complainant is son of the present applicant and he had purchased a house in the Radhakrishna Bungalow from the builder by paying amount of consideration of Rs.8,10,240/- and since more than two years is residing in the said bungalow along with the family.
For the purpose of purchase of the said property he has also obtained loan from the bank and said loan is still running in his name in the bank.
The complainant is residing in the joint family along with his parents and brother and sister-in-law.

After lapse of certain period of time, the complainant as well as his brother and his mother has come to know that the sister-in-law of the complainant is not having good character and therefore they NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4065/2018 ORDER DATED: 09/01/2025 undefined have tried to obtain divorce of his brother from his sister-in- law and the applicant herein is trying to create obstructions in the said process.
Therefore, disputes have been started to be cropped up between the members of the family.

3.2. Even one month before the date of the incident, the father as well as sister-in-law of the complainant had gone after leaving the house and started to reside at different place by taking ornaments as well as money with them.

On the date of incident the complainant and his brother has gone to his village i.e. native place and at that relevant point of time without informing the complainant the applicant has entered into the house by breaking the lock of the house and he has put a new lock.
The said fact has come to the notice of the complainant on the basis of information by the watchman.
Therefore, present complaint is has been registered.

3.3. 
Pursuant to registration of the complaint, investigation has already been commenced and after recording the statement of the witnesses as well as carrying out necessary panchnama, the Investigating Officer concerned thought it fit that prima facie offence is made out and therefore submitted NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4065/2018 ORDER DATED: 09/01/2025 undefined charge sheet before the competent court which ultimately culminated into Criminal Case No.1663 of 2010 pending before the learned Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Court No.17,

6. So far as other offences are concerned, Mr.Shah, learned advocate has emphatically submitted that in fact at the time of investigation the investigating officer has recorded the statement of the witnesses.
If recitals of those statements are to be seen, tone and tenor of those statements would clearly show that the father of the complainant is applicant herein.

On the very next day, on the basis of another key available with the complainant, the house was opened and they have started residing in the said house and since then they are residing in the said house.

8. Before dwelling into the issue involved int eh present matter, I would like to put reliance upon certain case laws.
At this stage, I may refer to the parameters laid down by this Court for quashing of an FIR in the case of State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, AIR 1992 SC 604.

entities.text: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, AIR 1992 SC 604
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The parameters are:-
"(1) Where the allegations made in the first information report or the complaint, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused.

(2) Where the allegations in the first information report and other materials, if any,
accompanying the FIR do not disclose a cognizable offence, justifying an investigation by police officers under Section 156(1) of the Code except under an order of a Magistrate within the purview of Section 155(2) of the Code.
(3) Where the uncontroverted allegations made in the FIR or complaint and the evidence collected in support of the same do not disclose the commission of any offence and make out a case NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4065/2018 ORDER DATED: 09/01/2025 undefined against the accused.
(4) Where, the allegations in the FIR do not constitute a cognizable offence but constitute only a non-cognizable offence, no investigation is permitted by a police officer without an order of a Magistrate as contemplated under Section 155(2) of the Code.

(5) Where the allegations made in the FIR or complaint are so absurd and inherently improbable on the basis of which no prudent person can ever reach a just conclusion that there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.

(6) Where there is an express legal bar en-grafted in any of the provisions of the Code or the concerned Act (under which a criminal proceeding is instituted) to the institution and continuance of the proceedings and/or where there is a specific provision in the Code or the concerned Act, providing efficacious redress for the grievance of the aggrieved party.

(7) Where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with malafide and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal Muninder Bhimsen Chorasiya vs State Of Gujarat on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102311947/
4 grudge."

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid observations of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, this Court is of the view that the case of the present applicant falls within the parameters cited in the above referred decisions.
11. Further, it is the settled position of law that criminal proceedings lodged based upon police report cannot be scattered.
Those powers can be exercised sparingly in a conscious manner and in a rarest of rare cases.

12. Herein the present case, having gone through the submissions made and the material available on record, prima facie, it is found out that if the prosecuting agency is to be NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4065/2018 ORDER DATED: 09/01/2025 undefined directed to continue with the proceedings which ultimately leads to gross abuse of process of law and injustice to the parties, in that event, those proceedings can be quashed and set aside and extra ordinary inherent powers can be exercised.

Secondly if bare perusal of the papers shows that there is legal bar against the institution of the continuation of the prosecution, in that event, the prosecution lodged against the applicant can be terminated.

If the allegations/acquisitions leveled against the applicant accused in the body of the FIR are to be taken on its face value and accepted in their entirety, they do not constitute the offence alleged and there is no legal evidence adduced or the evidence adduced clearly or manifestly fails to prove the charge.

13. Considering the submissions made and the material available on record as well as the relevant provisions of law, basic ingredients to attract provisions of Section 341 of the Indian Penal Code as well as provisions of Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code do not appear to be satisfied.
In that event, the prosecution lodged against the applicant is required to be quashed.
